headline: No live signal. Full 24-trade ledger still net-negative (-2.7 bps/trade); rolling 13-bet window positive (+9.5 bps) on recent shorts.
regime_note: BTC has re-rated to ~$77.7k from the $63-66k range that produced most of the ledger. The rolling window is dominated by a handful of shorts that worked during the Aug 21-23 pullback — regime-favorable, not proven edge.
assessment_md:
**Status: no active position; sample still too thin to draw conclusions.**

The strategy remains selective and slow to accumulate data. The full ledger now shows **24 resolved trades, 37.5% win rate, and -2.7 bps net per trade (-64.4 bps cumulative)** — i.e. across all live trades it has *lost* money after the assumed 3 bps cost. That's consistent with what validation warned: the gross edge (~4 bps) barely clears realistic costs, so it is likely not net-profitable.

**What changed vs last time:** one new trade was added (Aug 23, +4.7 bps net). The rolling 13-bet window looks healthy — **84.6% wins, +9.5 bps net** — but that window is dominated by a cluster of shorts that paid off during BTC's Aug 21-23 pullback from ~$78k (single trades of +48.7, +16.2, +13.0 bps). A few lucky fades in a favorable regime is not evidence of durable edge.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us:** 24 trades is far too few to distinguish skill from noise — the swing from a negative full ledger to a positive recent window is exactly the kind of variance you expect at this sample size. Note also `edge_search_survivors: 0`: no variant clears the stricter two-venue, 5 bps-cost bar.

**Bottom line:** Behaving roughly as expected for a marginal strategy. No degradation alert warranted, but no proven profitability either. Keep collecting data; don't read the hot streak as confirmation.
